source.version: Journal version of record, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1910545, published 14 September 2026 (received 16 June 2026, revised 29 July 2026, accepted 17 August 2026), doi 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1910545
source.title_on_document: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning

supplement.where: No supplementary material or appendix is cited. Instruction scripts, system prompt, prompt-template pool, model version, and rating rubric are available from the corresponding authors on request (p. 5, Section 2.5).
supplement.holds: Nothing statistical; all reported statistics are in the main text, Tables 1-4, and Figure 2.

paper_design_summary: Adults who use generative AI, recruited on an online participant platform (students and early-career workers), were randomized to three arms for an argumentative essay: a self-generation-first 'autonomous' AI workflow, a direct-adoption 'dependent' AI workflow, or no AI (Phase 1). Then, 15-20 minutes later in the same session, everyone wrote a parallel essay with no AI (Phase 2). Two blind raters scored each essay on 1-7 rubrics for reasoning quality (primary), idea diversity, and originality.

studies.label: Three-arm workflow experiment (argumentative essays, AI-assisted Phase 1 then unaided Phase 2)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Offloading manner for the Phase-1 essay: autonomous AI workflow (draft and submit own thesis and outline before the AI panel unlocks, then compare and rewrite), dependent AI workflow (adopt AI output with minimal change), or no AI. Topic and phase order were counterbalanced across participants.
assignment.quote: Participants were assigned by stratified block randomization (strata: baseline-ability tertile crossed with student or worker status; block size six; equal allocation), with the assignment sequence generated and recorded by the online system.
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 3, Section 2.1.1: 'The study was not formally preregistered'; decisions fixed in a dated internal analysis plan written before the data were analyzed

arms.name: Autonomous
arms.description: Self-generation-first workflow: interface step-lock required a written position and 3-5 point outline (at least 80 characters) before the AI panel opened; then compare own outline with the model's points, record at least one disagreement, judge which is better founded, and rewrite in own words.

arms.name: Dependent
arms.description: Direct-adoption workflow: 'Use AI to complete this argumentative essay... adopt the AI output as it stands, with minimal changes.' No outline step.

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Wrote Phase-1 essay independently with no AI tool, search engine, or external material.

participants.exclusions: 241 of 900 excluded after assignment: failed attention check (89), did not complete Phase 2 (95), flagged by the research team's AI-use screen in the no-AI arm only (69), long-string responding (10); categories overlap. Excluded by arm: 56 autonomous, 69 dependent, 116 no-AI (20.1, 23.5, 35.4 percent; chi2(2) = 20.22, p < 0.0001). Paper calls the primary analysis modified intention-to-treat. Sensitivity: all 805 with a Phase-2 essay; all 900 via multiple imputation; per-protocol n = 585 (172/201/212).
participants.who: Adults who reported using generative AI for cognitive tasks, recruited through an online research participant platform with quotas across student and early-career-worker status; mean age 24.6 years, 54 percent women; Chinese-speaking.
participants.country: Not stated explicitly; Chinese-speaking participants, Chinese-language instructions, ethics approval from Zhengzhou University (China)
participants.quote: leaving a primary analysis sample of N = 659 (autonomous = 222, dependent = 225, no-AI = 212; mean age 24.6 years, 54% women).
participants.locator: p. 3, Section 2.2; p. 4, Table 2; p. 13, Section 4.5

ai_tool.name_model: Qwen3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen; Alibaba Cloud) via official API, one pinned model version, fixed sampling parameters, identical general-purpose Chinese writing-assistant system prompt in both AI arms
ai_tool.how_used: AI panel inside the study platform drawing on a shared prompt-template pool; number of calls uncapped (range 1-8, median 3). Workflows enforced by interface locks: autonomous arm had to submit own position and outline first and then critique and rewrite; dependent arm instructed to generate the essay with AI and adopt it with minimal change. AI available only in Phase 1; Phase 2 prohibited AI for all arms.

task.description: Argumentative essays of 300-500 words on public-policy questions (Topic A: banning private cars from city centers; Topic B: moving from a 5-day to a 4-day work week), topic and phase counterbalanced. Unaided baseline essay (120-200 words, homework policy) before randomization used as a covariate.
task.duration: Baseline essay 5-7 min; Phase 1 12-15 min limit; Phase 2 10-12 min limit, 15-20 min after Phase 1 in the same session

outcomes.name: Phase-2 (unaided) reasoning quality
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric: clarity of thesis, relevance and sufficiency of evidence, coherence of reasoning, handling of counterarguments. At least two trained raters blind to condition and phase (third rater for disagreements of 2+ points); rater mean used; ICC(2,k) = 0.86. Raters' background not stated. ANCOVA adjusting baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time. Robustness variants in Table 4 (per-protocol, HC3, single raters, Phase-1 adjustments, relaxed exclusions, multiple imputation n = 900) and change-score comparison vs baseline essay (p. 12).
outcomes.delay: 15-20 minutes after the AI-assisted Phase 1, same session

contrasts.reported: adjusted difference = -0.38, 95% CI [-0.59, -0.18], d = -0.28, two-sided p = 0.0002, FDR q = 0.0006 (n = 659); HC3 robust SE = 0.10, p = 0.0002; per-protocol -0.41 [-0.62, -0.20], n = 585; multiple imputation -0.39 [-0.57, -0.21], n = 900. Adjusted arm means in Figure 2A only.
contrasts.locator: p. 7, Section 3.4; p. 8, Figure 2; p. 9, Sections 3.5-3.6; p. 10, Table 4

contrasts.reported: +0.21 [95% CI [0.01, 0.41], 90% CI [0.04, 0.38]]; uncorrected two-sided p = 0.042, does not survive FDR correction (q = 0.12); labeled exploratory
+0.59 (d = 0.45, p < 0.0001, FDR q < 0.0001); with Phase-1 time adjustment +0.63 (p < 0.0001)
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Section 3.4; p. 9, Section 3.5; p. 8, Figure 2B

outcomes.name: Phase-2 (unaided) idea diversity
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric, 'idea diversity captured the number and breadth of distinct perspectives' within each essay (within-essay variety, not similarity across people). Blind raters, ICC(2,k) = 0.81. ANCOVA adjusting baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time; FDR within three-outcome family. With Phase-1 time adjustment, dependent vs no-AI unchanged (-0.30, q = 0.006).
outcomes.delay: 15-20 minutes after the AI-assisted Phase 1, same session

contrasts.reported: No number in text; Figure 2B point estimate about +0.45 with 95% CI entirely above zero ('the autonomous-dependent interval entirely above it')
contrasts.locator: p. 8, Figure 2B and caption; p. 8, Section 3.4 last sentence

outcomes.name: Phase-2 (unaided) originality
outcomes.question: after_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric, 'originality captured novelty relative to templated answers'. Blind raters, ICC(2,k) = 0.79. ANCOVA adjusting baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time; FDR within three-outcome family.
outcomes.delay: 15-20 minutes after the AI-assisted Phase 1, same session

contrasts.reported: No number in text; Figure 2B point estimate about +0.2 with 95% CI spanning zero ('all originality intervals span zero')

outcomes.name: Phase-1 (AI-assisted) reasoning quality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Same 1-7 reasoning rubric, blind raters, ICC(2,k) = 0.85. Only the two AI arms are compared; the paper says Phase-1 scores in the AI arms rate a human-model product and are not comparable to the no-AI arm, and reports no AI vs no-AI Phase-1 contrast.

contrasts.reported: adjusted difference = +0.78, 95% CI [0.60, 0.96], p < 0.0001, d = 0.75; survived FDR

outcomes.name: Phase-1 (AI-assisted) idea diversity
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric, number and breadth of distinct perspectives within the essay; ICC(2,k) = 0.84. AI arms only.

outcomes.name: Phase-1 (AI-assisted) originality
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 1-7 rubric, novelty relative to templated answers. AI arms only. Phase-1 originality ICC not separately reported (Section 3.3 lists Phase-1 reasoning and diversity, Phase-2 reasoning, diversity, originality).

company_involvement.description: Authors declare no commercial or financial relationships; the AI model (Qwen3.5, Alibaba Cloud) was accessed through its public API. Funding from Chinese government and university grants.
company_involvement.locator: p. 13, Funding; p. 14, Conflict of interest

data_and_code.data_url: Not public; de-identified data and analysis materials available from the corresponding authors on reasonable request (p. 13, Data availability statement)

eligibility.reason: Individuals were randomized (stratified block randomization) to two generative-AI workflows or no AI; 900 randomized and 659 analyzed. Blind raters scored originality and idea diversity on the essays. Main creativity-relevant estimates are after_ai (Phase 2, AI removed). The with_ai Phase-1 contrasts are only between the two AI workflows (ai_design). The task is argumentative essays, and the primary outcome is reasoning quality, not creativity, so whether the task counts as creative is a judgment call.

one_line_finding: On an unaided essay written 15-20 minutes after one AI-assisted essay, the direct-adoption arm scored below no-AI on reasoning quality (-0.38, d = -0.28, p = 0.0002) and idea diversity (-0.30, d = -0.23, p = 0.004) but not originality (-0.07, d = -0.02, q = 0.28); the self-generation-first arm did not fall below no-AI (p. 7-8, Section 3.4, Figure 2).
open_questions: Does an argumentative policy essay count as a creative task? Originality and idea diversity are rated, but the paper's primary outcome is reasoning quality.
Idea diversity is rated within each essay (number and breadth of perspectives), so it is coded flexibility, not across-people diversity.
Codebook rule 3 (arm closest to free chatbot use) does not settle which AI arm is primary for ai_vs_bau: both arms are instructed extremes. The paper's own primary contrast is dependent vs no-AI.
No AI vs no-AI contrast is reported for Phase 1 (with_ai); only autonomous vs dependent.

The no-AI arm lost 116 of 328 (35.4 percent), 69 of them through a single-consensus AI-use screen applied only to that arm; the paper reports the contrast with these participants restored (-0.38, n = 713) and with multiple imputation over all 900 (-0.39).
Rater background (expert or lay) not stated; coded human_raters.
notes: Arm-level means and SDs for outcomes are not printed; only adjusted differences, d, p or q values, and Figure 2A bar charts of covariate-adjusted means (error bars +/-1 SE). Autonomous-vs-dependent Phase-2 differences for idea diversity and originality appear only in Figure 2B. Originality dep vs no-AI prints raw -0.07 with d = -0.02, recorded as printed. Trait (ACO, H3) and mediation analyses (metacognitive monitoring, intrinsic motivation) and process-log indices are not outcomes scored on the output and are omitted. Phase-2 n_analyzed is 659 (222/225/212); Phase-1 AI-arm comparison implies 447 people (t(445) in fidelity check, p. 7).
